newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zairean rebels said advancing on three fronts.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebels said advancing on three fronts.

text.p: Zairean rebels on Monday advanced on three fronts towards a heavily fortified eastern airport and army base at Kindu, a senior rebel official said.

Bishikwabo Chubaka, rebel-appointed governor of South Kivu and a senior official in the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL), told Reuters the rebels hoped to expel Zaire's ragged army out of Kindu town very soon.
Kindu, a mining town, also has a large French-built airport and is 340 km (200 miles) west of the lakeside rebel-held town of Bukavu on the border with Rwanda.

Chubaka said ADFL forces were moving towards Kindu from around the tin and gold mining town of Punia, where fighting was reported by both sides on Saturday, and from the southeastern Lake Tanganyika port of Kalemie through the town of Kabambare.
He said the rebels did not foresee major problems in capturing the small garrison at Kabambare and then moving on.
"We are moving towards Kindu on the three fronts. We soon hope to be in Kindu," said the governor, adding rebels were also pursuing troops towards the Lake Tanganyika town of Moba.
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila said on Sunday his forces were 25 km (15 miles) outside Moba, which the government was reinforcing by railway and air from the military base at Kamina.
Kabila, fighting to overthrow ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko, said rebels had captured Bafwasende, 250 km (150 miles) east of Kisangani, the base for a government counter-offensive.
Chubaka said Kindu was defended by Zairean troops and Hutu former Rwandan troops and Interahamwe militiamen who fled to eastern Zaire in 1994 in fear of reprisals for their role in the 1994 genocide.
Kindu and Kisangani are the only two airports held by government forces in eastern Zaire. The other airports at Bunia, Goma, Bukavu, Uvira, Kamanyola and Kalemie are held by rebels.
The AFDL says it stopped advancing towards a refugee camp at Tingi Tingi to allow the U.N. refugee agency to work out a plan to repatriate more than 120,000 Rwandan refugees trapped there.
Kabila's rebels say they have seized an eastern border strip about 1,400 km (875 miles) long since their revolt began in October.

U.N. officials said a U.N. team flying over eastern Zaire spotted a group of between 15,000 and 20,000 refugees on Sunday at Kalima west of Shabunda, which Kinshasa said its forces recaptured last week but rebels say is still in their hands.
They said church groups outside of Kindu were prepared to distribute what medicine and food was brought in but it was not known how long the refugees would stay.

Michelle Quintaglie, a spokeswoman for the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP), said agencies planned to distribute food on Monday to thousands of refugees who fled to Tingi Tingi last week to escape fighting.
She said foreign aid workers were returning daily to Tingi Tingi but were pulling back to Kisangani city before dark. The last international aid staff based there left last Friday.
